wards.name: the reading door
wards.denied: A door of banded oak with no handle on this side. It was made to be opened from within, by somebody who is not answering.
wards.opened: The door gives at the hinge and swings the wrong way entirely.

spots.line: The deep presses. Nothing here has been read in living memory, and all of it has been kept.
Shelves cut into the rock itself, and the rock is dry, which is the whole point.
A chair, pushed back, and a book open on the desk at a page somebody stopped at.
Lamps in a line down the middle, all of them lit, none of them by you.
The stair. Counting the steps on the way down is a habit people pick up here.

chests.line: A chest of things too odd to shelve and too good to burn.
The librarian's own press, and the librarian has been gone some time.
Past the door, at the back of the deep presses, in a box that was never meant to come out.

people.name: Keeper Ilde
chatter: Down here it is dry and it is cold and nothing rots. That is the only reason any of it survives.
The door has been shut since before I took the post. I have never asked who shut it.
You may read anything on this side of it. That is a great deal already.
Do not bring a naked flame past the third lamp.

people.name: Odger, who dusts
chatter: Twelve years dusting. I have read more of it than she has.
Some of the shelves are warm. Only some. Always the same ones.
If you hear pages turning, it is a draught. It is always a draught.
